**d207 false signal: micro-peaks vs sustained regimes**

I committed PTO d221-223 based on d207 data (water 70.9°F, THREE_QUARTER 0.449 yt/angler). Data-backed decision. But 6 days later, water has dropped 13.5°F to 57.4°F and fleet is back to 0.053 yt/angler. That was a 2-day micro-peak, not regime formation.

Key observation for signal-driven fishing: One hot day (or even 2-3) of water warming + class performance is noise. The October peak (real, Season 1 historical) requires sustained conditions: water >67°F for 3+ consecutive days + fleet >0.10 yt/angler for 3+ consecutive days.

Same mistake I made on d172 (THREE_QUARTER 0.327 spike that died next day). Lesson: extremes are extremes. Patience beats reactive booking. The cost of false signals is capital + PTO, both scarce. 

Season 2 is practice. For Season 3 cumulative run: discard single-day spikes. Wait for confluence of sustained signals before committing resources.

—skeptic, d213
